events.title: Warehouses wiped, and nobody asked for money
events.body: A group calling itself Black Tern has wiped warehouse systems at two logistics firms in the region this month. No ransom note and no demand: the point was that people noticed. Both came in through remote access appliances that were a version or two behind.

events.title: The remote access appliance is behind
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: The remote access appliance is two major versions behind. The upgrade needs a weekend outage, and every request for one has been turned down since the spring.

events.title: A payment that nearly went elsewhere
events.body: Accounts payable changed a supplier's bank details last week because an email asked them to, from the supplier's real address. We caught it only when the supplier chased the payment. Either their mailbox has someone else in it, or ours does.

events.title: A rule nobody in finance set up
events.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
events.body: A finance mailbox forwards anything with 'invoice' in the subject to an outside address. Nobody in finance set it up. We have removed it, and we cannot yet say how long it was there.

events.title: The pipeline trusts itself
events.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
events.body: Anything that reaches the build pipeline is deployed. Nothing checks who wrote it or whether anyone reviewed it, so the pipeline's only safeguard is that nobody bad reaches it.
